2607.23581.title: Verification-Notebook Learning for Source-Aware Multimodal Misinformation Detection
2607.23581.paper_summary: Multimodal misinformation verification is challenging because misleading signals may come from different parts of a post and require different forms of evidence. LVLMs are well suited to this task, but their verification performance often depends on the inference procedure applied to each instance. Existing methods improve this procedure through stronger prompting, retrieval, or deliberation, but rarely retain the verification patterns learned from previous examples. We propose Verification-Notebook Learning (VNL), a non-parametric framework that learns an external verification procedure for a frozen LVLM before inference. VNL builds a compact notebook of decision principles, evidence cues, and recurring pitfalls from prior verification experience. The notebook remains fixed during inference and guides the verification of new examples. Rather than updating model parameters or storing demonstrations, VNL records learned knowledge in an artifact that can be inspected directly. Experiments show that VNL consistently outperforms a range of competitive baselines. Further analyses show that the Verification Notebook improves fine-grained source attribution while remaining compact and interpretable, providing an effective way to accumulate verification knowledge without model training.
2607.23581.paper_summary_zh: 多模態錯誤資訊驗證具有挑戰性，因為誤導性信號可能來自帖文的不同部分，並需要不同形式的證據。LVLMs 非常適合這項任務，但它們的驗證性能通常依賴於應用於每個實例的推理過程。現有的方法通過更強的提示、檢索或深思來改進這一過程，但很少保留從先前示例中學到的驗證模式。我們提出了驗證筆記本學習（VNL），這是一個非參數框架，在推理之前為凍結的 LVLM 學習外部驗證程序。VNL 建立了一個緊湊的決策原則、證據線索和來自先前驗證經驗的重複陷阱的筆記本。該筆記本在推理過程中保持固定，並指導新示例的驗證。VNL 並不是更新模型參數或存儲示範，而是將學到的知識記錄在一個可以直接檢查的工件中。實驗表明，VNL 始終超越一系列競爭基準。進一步的分析顯示，驗證筆記本在保持緊湊和可解釋的同時改善了細粒度的來源歸屬，提供了一種有效的方式來積累驗證知識而無需模型訓練。
